blueprint.title: Night-shift Metrics Relay Outage
blueprint.scenario: A Node.js metrics relay service collects tagged log lines from upstream producers, aggregates per-minute counters and percentiles, then re-emits them as newline-delimited JSON over a TCP socket. The on-call SRE woke to a PagerDuty alert at 3 AM: Datadog shows a flat line on all dashboards and the relay's own health endpoint is returning stale timestamps. The repo (~1,400 lines across eight source files) shipped a rushed feature-iteration commit six hours ago that added tag-cardinality limiting and a percentile approximation algorithm. The service appears to start and accept connections, but downstream consumers receive either malformed frames or silent zeros.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
```
[PAGERDUTY] 03:14 CRITICAL metrics-relay health-check latency=stale, downstream=flatline
$ journalctl -u metrics-relay --since '1 hour ago' | tail -40
Oct 12 02:47:01 node[3821]: INFO  relay starting on :9900 (aggregation) :9901 (sink)
Oct 12 02:47:01 node[3821]: INFO  tag limiter active, max_cardinality=200
Oct 12 02:47:12 node[3821]: WARN  flush #1: 0 series emitted
Oct 12 02:47:22 node[3821]: WARN  flush #2: 0 series emitted
Oct 12 02:47:32 node[3821]: WARN  flush #3: 0 series emitted
...
Oct 12 02:58:44 node[3821]: ERROR frame encode: buf.write is not a function
Oct 12 02:58:44 node[3821]: WARN  flush #72: 0 series emitted
```

The metrics relay at `/app/relay/` is broken after last night's feature push. Producers send tagged log lines over TCP to port 9900. Every 10 seconds the relay must flush aggregated metrics—counts, sum, p50, p95, p99—as length-prefixed newline-delimited JSON frames to any consumers connected on port 9901. A frame's 4-byte big-endian length prefix must exactly match the byte length of the JSON payload that follows. Each flush must emit one JSON object per distinct metric name+tag-set combination seen in that window; zero-count series must be dropped. The p50/p95/p99 fields must be computed with a t-digest-style interpolation over bucketed samples (the bucket configuration is already present in the codebase). Tag cardinality limiting must enforce a per-metric-name cap: once a metric has seen `max_cardinality` distinct tag-sets, new tag-sets for that metric are silently dropped (existing ones still accumulate). The relay must recover from upstream producer disconnects and continue serving consumers without restart. Bring the service to a state where it correctly handles all of these behaviors; the verifier will connect producers and consumers over the real TCP protocol and check frame correctness across multiple flush windows with varied cardinality, disconnects, and percentile distributions.
requirements: Port 9900 accepts producer TCP connections sending tagged log lines in the format: `<metric_name> <value> <tag1=v1>[,<tag2=v2>...]\n`
Port 9901 accepts consumer TCP connections and receives flushed frames every 10 seconds
Each frame consists of a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer (byte length of the following payload) immediately followed by the UTF-8 JSON payload
The 4-byte length prefix must exactly equal the byte length of the JSON string that follows it
Each flush emits one JSON object per distinct (metric_name, tag-set) combination observed in the current window
Each emitted JSON object contains fields: metric (string), tags (object), count (integer), sum (number), p50 (number), p95 (number), p99 (number)
Percentiles p50/p95/p99 are computed using the bucketed t-digest interpolation already configured in the codebase
Series with zero count in the current window are not emitted

Tag cardinality limiting: once a metric_name has accumulated max_cardinality distinct tag-sets, any incoming line with a new tag-set for that metric is silently dropped; existing tag-sets still accumulate values
The relay must survive upstream producer TCP disconnects and reconnects without requiring a restart
The relay must continue serving existing consumer connections across flush cycles
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm (Node.js 20 installed via apt/nodesource, pinned)

/app/relay/ contains ~1,400 lines across 8 source files: index.js (entry, TCP server setup), aggregator.js (flush loop, series management), frame.js (length-prefix encoder), percentile.js (t-digest bucket logic), tag_limiter.js (cardinality cap), parser.js (line parser), health.js (HTTP health endpoint), config.js (constants including max_cardinality=200, BUCKET_CONFIG array)

Bug 1 (not visible by reading alone — data-dependent): in frame.js the length prefix is computed as `payload.length` (character count) instead of `Buffer.byteLength(payload, 'utf8')` — invisible for ASCII-only inputs but breaks on any tag value containing a non-ASCII character (the verifier injects tag values with UTF-8 multi-byte chars like accented names); also the `buf.write` call uses incorrect argument order, causing the 'buf.write is not a function' error only when the Buffer is created with the wrong constructor path introduced by the feature commit

Bug 2 (interacting): in tag_limiter.js the cardinality check incorrectly uses a single global Map keyed only on metric_name instead of a Map<metric_name, Set<tag_set_key>> — this causes all metrics to share one cardinality counter; when the global counter hits max_cardinality all new tag-sets across ALL metrics are dropped, which (combined with the fact that the flush still increments its own counter) causes the flush to emit 0 series after the limiter fires, masking the frame encoding bug since no frames are ever sent; fixing only the frame bug leaves the cardinality bug causing silent data loss on multi-metric workloads; fixing only the cardinality bug lets the relay emit frames but they have wrong length prefixes for non-ASCII inputs

percentile.js is correct but requires the aggregator to call it with the right bucket accumulator object — the feature commit changed the accumulator shape in aggregator.js to an array instead of the object that percentile.js expects, so percentiles silently return 0 unless the aggregator is also fixed
A plausible but uninvolved monitoring.js (~120 lines) that logs internal queue depths — does not affect correctness
A plausible but uninvolved retry.js (~80 lines) for outbound HTTP health-push — not involved in TCP path
Service is pre-started via Docker CMD so the solver sees it running but producing zero output
Sample producer script /app/tools/producer.js and sample consumer /app/tools/consumer.js provided for manual testing
blueprint.internal_hint: Two interacting causes plus a third subtler issue: (1) tag_limiter.js uses a flat global counter shared across all metrics instead of per-metric Sets — once this fires, all series are dropped and 0 frames are sent, which masks bug 2. (2) frame.js computes the length prefix using `.length` (codepoint count) instead of `Buffer.byteLength(payload,'utf8')` AND has a broken Buffer constructor path from the feature commit causing the 'buf.write is not a function' error on first non-empty flush. Fixing bug 1 alone: relay starts emitting frames but with wrong length prefixes on UTF-8 tag values, causing consumer protocol parse failures. Fixing bug 2 alone: relay still silently drops everything due to bug 1, appears fixed in logs but no frames reach consumers. (3) aggregator.js passes a plain array as the accumulator to percentile.js which expects `{buckets: [...], count: N}` — percentiles are all 0. The solver must instrument the running service, observe the cardinality limiter firing (add logging or inspect state), fix the per-metric cardinality accounting, then observe frame encoding failures on UTF-8 inputs, then fix the Buffer construction and byte-length calculation, then notice percentiles are zero and fix the accumulator shape. The difficulty comes from: (a) bug 1 hiding bug 2 until bug 1 is fixed, (b) the frame bug only manifesting on non-ASCII tag values which the provided sample tools don't use but the verifier does, (c) the percentile bug being a data-shape mismatch not a logic error.
blueprint.trap: A shallow solver fixes the obvious 'buf.write is not a function' error (the logged error) by patching the Buffer constructor call but does not fix the byte-length calculation. Tests with ASCII-only tag values pass. The verifier then sends tag values with accented characters (e.g. `region=São_Paulo`, `env=München`), causing length prefix to be off by the number of extra UTF-8 bytes. Consumers parsing the stream get desynchronized and all subsequent frames are rejected. Additionally, a solver who fixes frame.js and tag_limiter.js but not the accumulator shape in aggregator.js will emit frames with p50=0/p95=0/p99=0 for all series, failing the percentile correctness tests.
tests: Test 1 (basic protocol): verifier connects a consumer to :9901, sends 50 ASCII log lines for 3 distinct metric+tag combos to :9900, waits 12 seconds, reads one flush frame; checks 4-byte big-endian prefix equals exact byte length of following JSON; checks JSON contains exactly 3 objects with correct metric/tags/count/sum

Test 2 (UTF-8 frame integrity): verifier sends lines with tag values containing multi-byte UTF-8 chars (accented city names); reads flush frame; checks prefix == Buffer.byteLength(payload,'utf8'); deserializes without error; checks count/sum correct

Test 3 (percentile correctness): verifier sends a known distribution (100 values uniformly spaced 1..100) for one metric; reads flush; checks p50 in [49,51], p95 in [94,96], p99 in [98,100] using the relay's own bucket resolution

Test 4 (cardinality limiting per-metric): verifier sends lines for metric_A with 250 distinct tag-sets and metric_B with 5 tag-sets; reads flush; checks metric_A has exactly 200 series (max_cardinality), metric_B has exactly 5 series (independent cap)
Test 5 (cross-metric isolation): verifier sends metric_A with 201 tag-sets and metric_B with 201 tag-sets; checks that both are independently capped at 200, not that the combined total is 200

Test 6 (producer disconnect recovery): verifier connects producer, sends 20 lines, closes TCP connection abruptly, waits 3 seconds, reconnects and sends 20 more lines; reads two consecutive flush frames; checks both frames are well-formed and second has count >= 20

Test 7 (zero-count series dropped): verifier sends lines in window 1, waits for window 2 with no new lines; reads window-2 flush; checks frame contains 0 JSON objects (empty payload) or no frame is sent
Test 8 (multiple consumers): verifier connects two consumers; producer sends 30 lines; checks both consumers receive identical well-formed frames in the same flush cycle
Test 9 (mixed workload): 8 metrics, varied cardinalities, UTF-8 tags, 3 flush windows observed; checks per-window correctness of counts, sums, and that p99 is non-zero for metrics with > 20 samples

verifier_knob.name: number of request scenarios
verifier_knob.effect: Dropping to 4 scenarios (basic protocol + one UTF-8 + cardinality + percentile) makes it solvable with only the two main bugs fixed; raising to 12+ adds more edge cases (concurrent producers, backpressure on slow consumers, very large tag-set strings) increasing required correctness depth

expected_failure_modes: Solver fixes the logged 'buf.write is not a function' error by using the correct Buffer API but keeps `.length` instead of `Buffer.byteLength`, passing all ASCII tests and failing UTF-8 frame tests
Solver fixes frame.js and tag_limiter.js but misses the aggregator.js accumulator shape mismatch, producing p50=p95=p99=0 on all series
Solver fixes tag_limiter.js (per-metric Sets) but misunderstands the cardinality-reset behavior and resets counts on each window instead of accumulating across the service lifetime

Solver observes zero output, checks the logs, patches only the tag limiter to raise max_cardinality to a huge number as a workaround — fixes the silence but leaves the frame encoding bug and the percentile bug
Solver verifies with the provided /app/tools/producer.js (ASCII only), sees frames flowing, declares done — misses UTF-8 breakage and percentile zeroes

speedrun: cat /app/relay/frame.js  # see payload.length bug + broken Buffer constructor causing logged error
cat /app/relay/tag_limiter.js  # see global flat Map shared across all metrics
cat /app/relay/aggregator.js  # see array accumulator passed to percentile.js
cat /app/relay/percentile.js  # confirm expects {buckets:[...], count:N} object shape

cat /app/relay/index.js  # confirm port setup, entry point
# Fix frame.js: replace payload.length with Buffer.byteLength(payload,'utf8'); fix Buffer constructor call
sed or direct edit of frame.js with correct Buffer.alloc(4) + buf.writeUInt32BE(Buffer.byteLength(payload,'utf8'),0)
# Fix tag_limiter.js: replace global Map with Map<metric_name,Set<tag_set_key>>
edit tag_limiter.js to use perMetricSets = new Map(); check/create Set per metric_name

invalid_failure_risks: Bug 1 is described as 'not visible by reading alone — data-dependent' but payload.length vs Buffer.byteLength is plainly visible in source; the difficulty lever is mislabeled
The 'buf.write is not a function' error is explicitly logged at runtime AND visible in source, making it trivially discoverable by two independent signals
A methodical agent reads all files before fixing anything, so the 'bug 1 masks bug 2' interaction has zero practical effect on agent behavior — all three bugs are found in one reading pass

The accented character test (Test 2) requires the verifier to inject non-ASCII tag values, but if the solver tests only with provided ASCII tools and the verifier catches it, the failure mode is valid — however the frame.js fix is still source-visible regardless

Test 7 (zero-count series dropped) is ambiguous: 'empty payload' vs 'no frame is sent' are two different behaviors, and the instruction doesn't specify which the relay should implement — both are listed as acceptable
The percentile bucket interpolation correctness (Test 3) depends on the solver not accidentally changing BUCKET_CONFIG while fixing aggregator.js — a minor risk of inadvertent breakage
Timing-dependent tests (Test 6 producer disconnect recovery, flush window timing) could be flaky if the container is under CPU load during the 10-second flush cycle
review.reasons: genuine_difficulty scores 2 because all three bugs are plainly visible by reading source code in a single pass (~15 commands), and the claimed 'data-dependent invisibility' of the frame.js bug is incorrect — `payload.length` vs `Buffer.byteLength` is an obvious source-level error additionally confirmed by the logged runtime error; a competent agent will read all files before touching anything, completely neutralizing the intended bug-interaction masking mechanic. The average score is approximately 3.8 but the genuine_difficulty floor of 4 is not met. Additionally, Test 7 has an ambiguity between 'empty frame' and 'no frame' as acceptable outputs.
fixes: Make at least one bug truly data-dependent and invisible from source: e.g., replace the obvious `payload.length` with a subtle off-by-one only triggered by specific bucket boundary conditions in percentile.js, or introduce a race condition in the flush timer that only manifests under concurrent producer connections
Remove the logged runtime error ('buf.write is not a function') or make it misleading — a logged error pointing directly at the broken line removes all difficulty from discovering bug 1

Increase the number of files to read and add plausible red-herring code paths (the monitoring.js and retry.js stubs are mentioned but should actually contain plausible-looking but incorrect implementations to cause the agent to waste time)

Make the bug-interaction masking mechanically effective: ensure a solver who reads only the logs (not all source files) would fix only the logged error and ship — this requires the frame.js bug to not be an obvious one-liner and the tag_limiter bug to not be in an obviously named file

Clarify Test 7: specify exactly whether a zero-series flush sends a 4-byte prefix of 0x00000000 followed by empty payload, sends nothing at all, or sends a special sentinel — this is a protocol detail that must be unambiguous for verifier correctness
